41.0.0.en: Ishmael went with ten men to visit Gedaliah, the governor of Judah, who was living at Mizpah. With him were also some of the royal court of King Zedekiah, whom Babylon had taken captive. Gedaliah welcomed them all and hosted them, and they ate with him at a great feast that he made for them. This shows Gedaliah’s love, his kindness of heart and his generosity.

41.1.0.en: It seems that Ishmael was jealous of Gedaliah and envied him the office of governor that he had received, and perhaps he had made a pact with the king of the children of Ammon to help him take the rule. So his visit to Gedaliah was for an evil purpose, and in the midst of the feast and the rejoicing he rose up and killed Gedaliah, the governor of Judah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed. This was not an ordinary murder, but carried two meanings:

41.1.1.en: 1- The killing of the head of the kingdom of Judah, which stirred up unrest among the people.

41.1.2.en: 2- A challenge to the king of Babylon, who had appointed Gedaliah.

41.2.0.en: The men of the palace were alarmed and afraid at the surprise, so Ishmael carried his evil further and struck down all the Jews, the men of Gedaliah, and all the Chaldeans who were assisting Gedaliah on behalf of Nebuchadnezzar. This shows Ishmael’s cruelty and wickedness, his boldness in evil, and also his deceit in exploiting hospitality and love as an opportunity for harm and evil.

41.2.1.en: The Jews grieved greatly over the killing of Gedaliah, and they appointed a fast for this in the seventh month (Zech 7:5; 8:19). This was most likely a year after Babylon’s seizure of Jerusalem and Judah, that is, in 586 BC.

41.2.2.en: May you thank everyone who shows you love, and repay good with good. If evil thoughts against someone fight against you, reject them and find an excuse for him, so that you keep your love for him and do not wrong anyone, even unintentionally. And if it happens, apologize quickly and make up with great love to the one you have wronged. [2] The capture and killing of the rest of the people (vv. 4-10):

41.2.3.en: 4- And it came to pass the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it, 5- That there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD. 6- And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. 7- And it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him. 8- But ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren. 9- Now the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain. 10- Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king’s daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.

41.3.0.en: Shechem: a city lying north of Jerusalem at a distance of 31.5 miles, at Mount Gerizim, and 5.5 miles south-east of Samaria.

41.3.1.en: Shiloh: 17 miles north of Jerusalem. It was the dwelling place of the Ark of the Covenant of God in the days of Eli the priest and for 300 years before that.

41.3.2.en: Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom of the Jews, which is called Israel and which comprises ten tribes. It lies about 35 miles north of Jerusalem.

41.3.3.en: Rent clothes: tearing the clothes is one of the signs of grief.

41.3.4.en: Cut themselves: wounded with deep cuts. Cutting the body to please the gods was one of the pagan customs.

41.3.5.en: After Ishmael killed Gedaliah, he and those with him hid his body in the palace, so that no one knew and the city would not be stirred up against him. On the day after the killing of Gedaliah, 80 men of the Jews happened to arrive from various places, namely Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria, which are Jewish places lying north of Jerusalem. They were going down south toward Jerusalem and reached Mizpah because it was on their way to Jerusalem. They were in mourning over the destruction of Jerusalem, as is proved by their tearing their clothes, but sadly they had been influenced by pagan worship and had cut their bodies. They wished to go to Jerusalem to present offerings to the Lord at the place where the temple of the Lord had been.

41.4.0.en: Ishmael went further in his evil and deceit. He went forward to meet these Jews who were coming in sorrow to visit the ruins of the temple of the Lord, and he too pretended to grieve over the destruction of the temple. He invited them to rest with Gedaliah at Mizpah and then continue their journey to Jerusalem.

41.5.0.en: The pit: a deep hole, which may hold water or mud, or may be dry.

41.5.1.en: Ishmael lured the 80 men into the middle of the city and surrounded them there with his men and began to kill them. He killed most of them and threw them into a pit that was near the middle of the city. It seems that the reason for their murder was to rob them of the goods they carried. This confirms Ishmael’s wickedness and greed, in contrast to the godly Gedaliah, who wanted to gather the scattered Jews and preserve them and their stability.

41.6.0.en: What confirms Ishmael’s greed is that ten of these eighty men noticed Ishmael plundering their possessions before killing them, so they asked him not to kill them in return for showing him their storehouses in their land, full of God’s good gifts, of crops and their produce. Ishmael agreed to satisfy his greed, whether these men were telling the truth or deceiving him, but by these words they were able to escape death.

41.7.0.en: Here the account tells us that the pit into which Ishmael threw the bodies of the men he had killed in the middle of the city had been made by King Asa, king of Judah, when he built the city of Mizpah after he prevailed over King Baasha, king of the kingdom of Israel (1 Kgs 15:22; 2 Chr 16:6).

41.8.0.en: The king’s daughters: all the women of the royal line who remained after the captivity of Zedekiah king of Judah and those with him and their deportation to Babylon. They may also have been of the household of Gedaliah, that is, his daughters and sisters, meaning the relatives of Gedaliah, the governor of the kingdom of Judah.

41.8.1.en: After Ishmael grew strong by killing many and the people feared him, he seized the men and women in Mizpah and took them captive. They went behind him as he left Mizpah and went to the kingdom of the children of Ammon. Among those he took captive were the princesses, the king’s daughters, that is, he took all the great ones of the city. This shows that he wanted to become king or governor. He went to the king of the children of Ammon to gain strength with the help of its king (Baalis).

41.8.2.en: Do not use your intelligence for evil to reach your goals, and let your means be sound in order to reach sound goals.

41.8.4.en: 11- But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done, 12- Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon. 13- Now it came to pass, that when all the people which were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad. 14- So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah. 15- But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites. 16- Then took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, even mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon: 17- And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt, 18- Because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land.

41.9.0.en: Gibeon: a city about five miles north of Jerusalem. The great waters: a deep pool more than ten meters deep.

41.9.1.en: The news reached Johanan the son of Kareah, the godly Jewish commander who had warned Gedaliah of the plot to assassinate him at the hand of Ishmael. Sadly, Gedaliah did not believe Johanan, and Ishmael killed him (ch. 40:13-16). Johanan gathered the captains of the Jewish forces, that is, the senior officers, and their soldiers, and advanced toward Mizpah to rescue his people from the hand of Ishmael. He overtook him before he reached the kingdom of the children of Ammon, at the city of Gibeon, which is about three miles from Mizpah, and met him at the deep pool of Gibeon.

41.10.0.en: When the captive Jews whom Ishmael had seized saw Johanan and the soldiers with him, they rejoiced and took courage. When Johanan, who had come to their aid, signaled to them, they left Ishmael, turned around all together and went after Johanan. As for Ishmael, he was in great fear when he saw Johanan and the army with him.

41.11.0.en: Since Ishmael feared Johanan and found with him only eight of the wicked men who followed him, he fled quickly to the children of Ammon. Thus the story of Ishmael, his plots and his evils came to an end.

41.12.0.en: Geruth Chimham: a Hebrew expression meaning “lodging place”. It is a place of hospitality established beside the city of Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, lying south of Jerusalem.

41.12.1.en: Johanan and the captains who followed him feared the wrath of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, when he would hear the news of the killing of his deputy Gedaliah, whom he had appointed governor over Judah. They had not wronged Gedaliah, but they feared Nebuchadnezzar’s fury against all the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah. So they fled with those who were with them to Egypt, away from Nebuchadnezzar, and rested on the way at Geruth Chimham. This was a weakness in Johanan despite his godliness. He ought to have prayed and asked Jeremiah, or recalled the words of Jeremiah, who had warned against taking refuge in Egypt. He should have believed in God and remained in his faith so that God would protect him.

41.12.2.en: Always take refuge in God through prayer and by asking the spiritual fathers, however logical your thinking may be, so that you do not slip onto a wrong path, and God will keep you and protect you in all your ways.

42.0.0.en: The leaders of the Jews and all the people, that is, a great multitude, came forward and went to Jeremiah the prophet so that he would pray for them, confessing their weakness, for they had become few in number after having been a great nation, because many had died at the hand of Babylon.

42.1.0.en: They also asked Jeremiah to guide them as to where they should go, whether to Egypt, or to Babylon, or remain in their land. Despite the appearance of concern to hear the voice of God, in truth they had already decided to go down to Egypt, as is evident from the previous chapter (ch. 41:17).

42.2.0.en: Jeremiah agreed to pray for them so that God would guide them as to where to go. Although they had said to him in (v. 2) “the LORD thy God”, Jeremiah answers them in (v. 4) “the LORD your God”, to teach them to be followers of their God, holding fast to Him and submitting to Him as His people.

42.3.0.en: They declared their obedience to the word of God that He would speak to Jeremiah, and their readiness to hear His voice, whether God’s opinion seemed good or hard to them. But sadly, all this was a superficial obedience, while the heart insisted on going down to Egypt.

42.3.1.en: May you believe that God’s choice is the best thing in your life, so that you obey God and the guidance of the Church, however hard it may be or contrary to your own opinions.

42.4.0.en: God waited ten days and then answered Jeremiah, for the following reasons:

42.4.1.en: 1- So that Jeremiah would pray and prepare to hear the voice of God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

42.4.2.en: 2- So that the people would prepare to hear the word of God, make ready to obey it, and be sure of their submission to Him.

42.5.0.en: Jeremiah sent for and called the leaders of the Jews, led by “Johanan”, and all the people who followed him.

42.6.0.en: Jeremiah told them that God had answered him concerning the counsel they had asked of him, whether to remain in the land or go down to Egypt.

42.7.0.en: God directed them to remain in their land and promised them the following:

42.7.1.en: 1- That He would build them and plant them, that is, establish them and make them grow, so that they would increase in strength and number.

42.7.2.en: 2- He also promises them that He would not pull them down or pluck them up, that is, that they would be established in the land and not be exposed to being driven out of it.

42.8.0.en: The third promise: if they remained in the land, the king of Babylon would not harm them, but they would live in tranquility and peace.

42.9.0.en: The fourth promise: that they would receive mercy and kindness from the king of Babylon. The fifth promise is that he would permit those whom he had taken captive to return to their land.

42.9.1.en: If you obey God’s commandments, you will enjoy mercies and blessings you cannot imagine, and you will live in peace and also grow in His love.

42.10.s.en: (3) The punishment for going down to Egypt

42.10.0.en: The sound of the trumpet: and exposure to death.

42.10.1.en: God warned them against going down to Egypt, thinking that there was safety there away from the hand of Babylon, because in their eyes Egypt was strong and would protect them, and they would not be exposed to wars or hunger but would live rejoicing in abundant good things.

42.11.0.en: God tells them the truth, which is that if they flee to Egypt they will be exposed to death by the sword that they think they are escaping by leaving their land, and they will also be exposed to death by hunger and will not find the abundant good things they expect in Egypt.

42.12.0.en: Thus by going down to Egypt they will be exposed to death, whether by the sword, by hunger or by disease.

42.13.0.en: God warns them that if they go down to Egypt they will be exposed to the wrath of God, who chastened Jerusalem and Judea by destruction and killing, and that He will chasten them in Egypt in the same way, that is, punish them for their disobedience and lack of repentance.

42.13.1.en: May you trust in God and not in the passing powers of the world. God’s commandment protects you, and trust in Him supports you however much troubles rise against you. On the contrary, all the powers of the world that you think support you collapse little by little before you.

42.14.s.en: (4) A warning against going down to Egypt

42.14.0.en: God forbids them, with a clear warning, to go down to Egypt, so that they would not perish.

42.15.0.en: He reminds them of their sin, which was lying and deceit when they asked God’s counsel about going down to Egypt or remaining in their land, while they were insisting in their heart on going down to Egypt.

42.16.0.en: He repeats His warning to them of death if they continue to insist on going down to Egypt.

42.16.1.en: If you sin, repent quickly and do not persist in the snare, because God loves you and repeats His call to you to repent, so that you may save yourself by returning to Him.

42.16.2.en: Jeremiah in Egypt and his prophecy about it
